method.method_draft: First parse the visual equation as a fitted linear model of the form \(\hat y=a+bx\), so the coefficient multiplying \(x\) is the slope estimate, \(\hat\beta=b=0.09\). From the written prompt, take the hypothesized population slope under \(H_0\) as \(0\) and the reported estimated standard deviation of the slope estimator as \(0.76\). Treat the test statistic as the standardized distance between the observed slope estimate and the null slope: observed departure \(=0.09-0=0.09\); divide by its standard error \(0.76\), giving \(0.09/0.76\approx0.12\).
